unsupported_claims: The method's optimization relies on eigendecomposition when the single hidden-layer network is linear with squared-error loss; this accepts the false premise and attributes conditions to the method that the passage does not contain.
A fixed or random hidden-layer case reduces to least squares via pseudoinverse, presented as a condition under which the method uses eigendecomposition instead of SGD; this is not in the evidence.
rationale: The answer goes along with the false premise and invents conditions under which the method replaces SGD with eigendecomposition. The source says the objective is optimized by SGD akin to backpropagation, and that eigendecomposition belongs to classic PCA/MDS approaches. The closing admission that it could not identify the method does not correct the premise.
